what: SentinelOne sells endpoint security: software agents on laptops, servers and cloud machines that spot and stop attacks automatically, with a platform that stores and searches the security data behind them.
customers: Enterprises and mid-sized companies, and managed security providers reselling the platform.
money: endpoint, cloud and data security agents by seat
moat: Agents installed across every machine a company owns, with detection models tuned to that environment. Replacing them means re-rolling software to every device.
risks: A $340M net loss on $1.1B of revenue, largely stock compensation
CrowdStrike and Microsoft are both larger and bundle more
The analyst average target is about where the shares trade
opportunities: Revenue grew from $205M to $1.0B in four years
$629M of cash against $15M of debt, and free cash flow has turned positive at $57M
Its data platform competes with security log tools priced far higher, which is a second market
watch: Annual recurring revenue growth and whether free cash flow keeps expanding.
